result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.local_reaching_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the local reaching centrality of every node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L41375-L41454){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.local_reaching_centrality( weighted=None, normalized=True, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Local reaching centrality](/assets/graphs/local-reaching-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-node directed out-tree, like an org chart: A heads B and C, and B heads D and E. Each node is shaded by the share of the other four nodes it can reach. A reaches all of them and scores 1.00, B reaches D and E for 0.50, and the leaves C, D and E reach no one and score 0." width="100%"} Local reaching centrality (Mones, Vicsek & Vicsek, 2012) measures how much of the network a node can reach, and how easily: - on an unweighted directed graph, it is the share of other nodes reachable from the node, which separates sources at the top of a hierarchy from sinks at the bottom - on an unweighted undirected graph, it averages `1 / distance` over all other nodes (unreachable ones count 0), like a normalized harmonic centrality - on a weighted graph, it averages the mean edge weight along the strongest path to each reachable node, where strong edges count as short (distance = total weight / weight) It is the building block of `global_reaching_centrality()`, which measures how hierarchical the whole network is. Values match NetworkX, which computes one node at a time. With weights, if several equally strong paths reach a node, their mean weights can differ, and the two libraries may pick different ones. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be positive. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : With weights, divide by the mean edge weight so scores are comparable across graphs. Default is `True`. Ignored without weights. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"local_reaching_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph has fewer than two nodes or no edges, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a reporting tree, the head of the organization reaches everyone and each leaf reaches no one: ::: {#38034b18 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec org = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["ceo", "cto", "cfo", "dev1", "dev2"]) .add_edges([("ceo", "cto"), ("ceo", "cfo"), ("cto", "dev1"), ("cto", "dev2")]) ) scores = org.local_reaching_centrality(return_dict=True) {org.get_label_from_id(n): s for n, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'ceo': 1.0, 'cto': 0.5, 'cfo': 0.0, 'dev1': 0.0, 'dev2': 0.0} ``` ::: :::
